classification.difficultyReason: Requires supplementary constructions and a geometric equal-area argument.

content.prompt: A rectangle is divided into six triangles as shown below. Show that the blue region has the same area as the orange region. Hint: You don’t need to calculate anything to show this.

spec.description: Six alternating triangles with unequal subdivisions; blue triangles have bases on the top edge and orange triangles have bases on the bottom edge.
spec.mathematics: A zigzag joins alternating points on the top and bottom of a rectangle, making six triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplementary vertical lines are visible in the question.

answer.short:
The blue and orange regions have equal area.

Draw vertical lines through the four interior zigzag vertices. Each resulting blue triangle has a matching orange triangle.
answer.worked: Draw vertical lines through the four interior zigzag vertices. Each vertical strip is a rectangle divided by a diagonal into one blue and one orange triangle. These two triangles have equal area. Pairing the triangles in all five strips shows that the total blue area equals the total orange area.

spec.description: The question figure with four vertical constructions through its interior zigzag vertices.
spec.mathematics: Five rectangular strips each contain an equal-area blue–orange pair.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplementary construction lines appear only in the solution.
